public_body: Soldiers' Home In Holyoke Board Of Trustees
overall: The AG found the Board violated the Open Meeting Law by entering executive session without the Chair's required declarations and by discussing a surplus-land vote in executive session that belonged in open session. Compliance ordered; no further remedy since minutes were already released.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the Board did not follow proper procedure to enter executive session at its June 2 and June 23, 2015 meetings.
allegations.key_passage: However, the Chair also failed to state that "an open meeting may have a detrimental effect on the negotiating position of the [Board]," as required by Purpose 6.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the Board discussed topics in executive session at its June 2 and June 23, 2015 meetings that were not appropriate for executive session.
allegations.key_passage: This discussion and vote should have occurred in open session, as doing so would not have harmed the Board's negotiating position.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law
remedy_passage: We order the Board's immediate and future compliance with the Law, and caution the Board that a similar, future violation may be considered evidence of an intentional violation of the Law.

source.publisher_filename: DETERMINATION - 4 5 2016 - OML 2016-47 - SOLDIERS' HOME IN HOLYOKE BOARD OF TRUSTEES.pdf

note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
